# Reviewed third-party sources

Only GLib 0.18.5 is vendored. It retains the exact published version and API; it is not relabeled as a newer fixed release. The registry archive SHA-256 is `233daaf6e83ae6a12a52055f568f9d7cf4671dabb78ff9560ab6da230ce00ee5`, checked against the prior Cargo.lock before import. Original VCS revision: `42b9caf98e03ded086362d9653ca58fe94dc8658`. [Published archive](https://static.crates.io/crates/glib/glib-0.18.5.crate).

The 121 published files are retained. Only `glib/src/variant_iter.rs` differs: two lines from [upstream soundness fix #1343](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core/pull/1343), merge `05dff0ee696f9bcd8617cd48c4b812d046d440cb`, make the C out-pointer mutable and pass `&mut p`. No new unsafe block, null-check workaround or unrelated modernization. The existing unsafe block now supplies the mutable out-argument required by the C API; borrowed results retain the original Variant lifetime. The exact local diff is in [patches/glib-0.18.5-variant-str-iter.patch](patches/glib-0.18.5-variant-str-iter.patch).

`manifest.json` records original and current file hashes, archive identity, patch digest, license and advisory disposition. `npm run check:vendor` checks all current source bytes, patch provenance and actual locked Cargo metadata; any missing/extra/changed file or an unreviewed non-workspace path dependency fails. This is a reviewed-content integrity check, not proof that modifying the manifest and sources together is trustworthy: both require code review against the original archive and upstream diff.

The upstream MIT license remains at [glib/LICENSE](glib/LICENSE), and the distributed static copy at [../public/licenses/glib.txt](../public/licenses/glib.txt). Build-generated dependency credits explicitly retain reviewed local third-party packages. Imported source formatting and inline upstream tests remain untouched; Prettier excludes `vendor/glib/`, and Rustfmt applies to authored workspace code. This formatting exclusion is not an advisory exemption.

## Verification and advisory visibility

- `npm run check:vendor`: offline provenance/locked-source check, also part of `tools/check.sh`. It does not need cargo-audit or GLib development libraries.
- `npm run audit:dependencies`: requires cargo-audit. Runs a fresh complete registry audit plus an explicitly labeled upstream-name/version assessment for vendored sources using one private RustSec snapshot. All reports are retained in ignored `target/quality/vendor-audit/report.json`; the product lockfile is never rewritten. New/unmapped local-source advisories, changed advisory metadata requiring reassessment, provenance errors and vulnerability matches fail this control. Known reviewed warnings remain printed; exit 0 is not campaign/security clearance.
- Linux: `cargo test -p phemios-glib-regression --locked --offline` and `cargo test -p phemios-glib-regression --release --locked --offline`. The crate has a Linux-only GLib dev dependency, no application runtime or Windows/macOS SDK requirement. `tools/check.sh` runs the optimized Linux cases after workspace tests.
- Optional macOS library verification, with GLib development libraries and pkg-config already installed: `node scripts/glib-regression.mjs` and `node scripts/glib-regression.mjs --release`. This disposable host harness imports the same test file and actual vendored library. It seeds its own lockfile with product versions, prunes it offline and writes only temporary files/ignored targets. It neither changes product resolution nor pretends to execute the Linux App. Windows is explicitly unsupported by this optional command.

Cargo-audit skips local source packages. RUSTSEC-2024-0429 therefore remains explicit in the supplemental inventory with **upstream affected version; upstream fix backported; Linux validation pending**. Do not remove that record merely because it vanishes from raw lockfile scanning. At the Lot 3a baseline, proc-macro-error and all three zbus-family notices remained unchanged. The subsequent macro correction is described below.

The maintainer owns this local backport. Any source/manifest/hash/disposition change must be reviewed and revalidated; new upstream fixes and advisories require follow-up. Remove the local patch when the native GTK/Tauri/WebKitGTK owners accept a compatible maintained fixed stack, with locked-tree and Linux regression/integration evidence. See [validation and remaining work](../docs/quality/lot-3a-validation.md).

## Macro diagnostic ports

Lot 3b imports published glib-macros 0.18.5 and gtk3-macros 0.18.2, preserving every original file/test and the MIT licenses. The exact original/current hashes and adapted patch digests are in manifest.json. The source ports derive from GLib c74a40a16b23a1b9c8e67842d32d02bc187f551d and GTK 45782251fa35ecf8bfe759ffceb3db32659a0c97, adjusted to the old 0.18 generated API and flags error paths. Cargo.toml.orig remains unmodified release provenance, including its historical macro-error declaration; normalized Cargo.toml is the active dependency manifest.

Both reviewed local sources remove the actual proc-macro-error dependency without adding a replacement. Upstream integration/unit/compile fixtures remain intact. New tests live outside imported source and exercise the real macros; the optional host runner now inherits all local source patches. `node scripts/macro-regression.mjs --fetch` bootstraps a disposable test-only manifest; subsequent runs are offline. Linux additionally compiles the real GTK expansion fixture. See [Lot 3b validation](../docs/quality/lot-3b-validation.md) for counts and pending native/Linux/minimum-toolchain acceptance.

All three local package identities remain in supplemental advisory matching. Removing proc-macro-error does not clear the GLib upstream advisory or the three D-Bus maintenance notices. Keep source hashes, patches, upstream tracking and warning disposition current, and remove local patches only when compatible native owners accept maintained published replacements with regression/integration evidence.

## keepawake Linux migration

Published keepawake 0.6.1 (21 exact archive files) is locally ported to zbus 6.1.0. Only normalized Cargo.toml and src/sys/linux.rs change. The local manifest declares Rust 1.89 and selects the Linux zbus Tokio/proxy/tracing features plus existing Tokio 1.53.3; version/public builder and all other original source/provenance files remain unchanged. The original Cargo.lock/Cargo.toml.orig still describe the published release, including its former D-Bus dependencies; they do not resolve the App. The complete original MIT license is distributed and the credits reader includes this local package.

This is a local source migration, not an upstream fix cherry-pick. Its patch records baseRevision plus reason instead of a fictitious upstreamCommit; source checks require exclusive, matching provenance and exact hashes. Reapplying the patch to the verified archive reproduces every current source byte. The private runtime bounds acquisition/authentication and cleanup, rolls back partial resources and logs release refusals without panicking. No new unsafe code or Mac/Windows backend change.

`node scripts/keepawake-regression.mjs --fetch` bootstraps a disposable, product-lock-seeded harness and two private dbus-daemon instances; subsequent runs can remain offline. It compiles the actual Linux module and tests cookie/FD lifetimes, refusal/disconnection/partial rollback, deadlines and nested-runtime callers. Linux runs it in the full gate; optional Mac execution establishes Unix protocol/module behavior, not Linux App/desktop acceptance. The service feature and mirrored private Options are test-only. See [Lot 4 validation](../docs/quality/lot-4-validation.md).

All four local package identities remain in supplemental advisory matching. The three retired D-Bus packages are removed from the real graph; GLib's upstream advisory remains explicit pending Linux validation. Maintain fresh upstream monitoring, patches/hashes/licenses and test evidence. Replace this local source with a compatible validated upstream keepawake release when available.

Git attributes preserve the exact LF/CRLF bytes of inventoried vendor source and original distributed license copies. Do not normalize those files: their byte hashes are part of provenance. This does not disable Git whitespace checks or advisory matching.
